title: Cap. IV Arg. 9 Sol close: general decree not sufficient certainty; Cap. IV Collocutors' args end
pass_a_gloss: Further, this foundation which we assert much more proves Christ constituted by God Savior and Head of those who will be saved, than that general one which is urged by these. For in that, All who will believe will be saved, a pact of salvation entered with the human race is shown on account of Christ; but which will lack effect unless the condition of believing is fulfilled by us; concerning which matter nothing is constituted in that decree. But when we defend that God has further decreed on account of Christ to give grace, faith, and life to all the elect, and from his fullness really to pour out into them this efficacious and saving grace: not by a bare pact, but by the very fact we make Christ Savior, and Head of all those who become partakers of salvation. Besides, that general decree, All believers will be saved, is not that decree of good pleasure on which our whole salvation rests. For this decree is, so to speak, declarative and doctrinal; but the salvation of singular persons ought to rest on a practical and operating decree of God. It would go miserably with us, if our whole salvation rested on this conditioned pact, If you shall have believed you will be saved, and there were not another decree of Divine good pleasure concerning faith to be given to us, and us to be efficaciously saved. Finally that general decree, All believers will be saved, cannot be for any singular person a sufficient foundation of certainty concerning his salvation. For that decree saves no one by its own virtue alone: Nay many will be damned who know and believe that all believers and repenting will be saved. There ought therefore to come for making certainty the efficacy of another decree; Namely, that I believe, that I will persevere even to the end. But whence this certainty of my faith, and of my perseverance? Not from my contingent free choice; therefore from some immutable Divine decree. If therefore we look at the thing, certainty of salvation as to this or that singular person ought to rest on some practical decree of God infallibly decreeing and operating the salvation of the same. If certain knowledge of the thing as to us: certainty of our salvation ought to rest on some revelation of the same decree, through the Spirit of adoption, and the effects of the same in the hearts of individuals. For that Spirit witnesses to our spirit that we are those sons of God, whom he destined to eternal life, and whom he has sanctified in this age, that he may glorify in the future. For the rest, in that universal decree promulgated after the manner of a law, Whoever shall have believed will be saved, neither can the certain salvation of any singular person be founded, nor anyone's certain knowledge of his salvation infallibly future. And these are all those arguments by which the Collocutors tried to establish the election of singular men from the antecedent condition of foresight faith. All of which have been taken from the writings of Arminius.
pass_b_english: Further: the foundation we assert proves far more that God constituted Christ Savior and Head of those who will be saved than their general one. All who will believe will be saved shows a pact of salvation with the human race for Christ's sake — but it lacks effect unless we fulfill the believing condition, about which that decree constitutes nothing. When we defend that God further decreed for Christ's sake to give grace, faith, and life to all the elect, and from his fullness really pour efficacious saving grace into them, we make Christ Savior and Head of all who share salvation not by bare pact but by the fact itself. Besides, All believers will be saved is not the good-pleasure decree our whole salvation rests on — it is, so to speak, declarative and doctrinal; singular persons' salvation must rest on a practical operating decree of God. It would go miserably with us if all our salvation rested on If you believe you will be saved, with no further good-pleasure decree to give us faith and save us efficaciously. Finally that general decree cannot be any singular person's sufficient certainty of his salvation: it saves no one by its own virtue alone — many will be damned who know and believe all believers and repenting will be saved. Certainty needs another decree's efficacy: that I believe, that I will persevere to the end. Whence that certainty of my faith and perseverance? Not from my contingent free choice — therefore from some immutable divine decree. As to the thing: certainty for this or that singular person rests on a practical decree infallibly decreeing and working that person's salvation. As to our knowledge: certainty rests on some revelation of that decree through the Spirit of adoption and its effects in individuals' hearts — that Spirit witnesses to our spirit that we are those sons of God destined to eternal life, sanctified in this age to be glorified hereafter. In the universal law-form decree Whoever believes will be saved, neither certain salvation of any singular person nor certain knowledge of one's infallibly future salvation can be founded. And these are all the Collocutors' arguments trying to establish election of singular men from the antecedent condition of foresight faith — all taken from Arminius's writings.
source_text: Porro, hoc fundamentum quod nos asserimus, multo magis probat Christum a Deo constitutum Salvatorem et Caput eorum qui servabuntur, quam illud generale quod ab istis urgetur. Nam in illo, Omnes qui credent salvabuntur, pactum salutis cum humano genere initum ostenditur propter Christum; sed quod effectu carebit nisi conditio credendi a nobis impleatur; qua de re in illo decreto nihil constitutum est. At quando defendimus, Deum insuper decrevisse propter Christum dare gratiam fidem et vitam omnibus electis, et ex plenitudine ejus realiter in eos diffundere hanc gratiam efficacem et salutiferam: non nudo pacto, sed ipso facto facimus Christum Salvatorem, et Caput eorum omnium qui fiunt salutis participes. Adhaec illud generale decretum, Omnes credentes salvabuntur, non est decretum illud εὐδοκίας cui tota salus nostra innititur. Nam hoc decretum est, ut sic dicam, declarativum et doctrinale; sed salus singularium personarum niti debet decreto Dei practico et operante. Misere ageretur nobiscum, si tota nostra salus niteretur hoc pacto conditionato, Si credideris salvus eris, et non esset aliud εὐδοκίας Divinae decretum de fide nobis danda, nobisque efficaciter servandis. Denique illud generale decretum, Omnes credentes salvabuntur, non potest esse alicui personae singulari fundamentum sufficiens certitudinis de salute sua. Nam illud decretum neminem servat sua sola virtute: Imo multi damnabuntur qui sciunt et credunt omnes credentes et resipiscentes fore salvandos. Accedat ergo oportet ad certitudinem faciendam alterius decreti efficacia; Nimirum, quod ego credam, quod ego in finem usque perseverabо. At unde haec certitudo fidei meae, et perseverantiae meae? Non a contingente meo libero arbitrio; ergo ab immutabili aliquo decreto Divino. Si igitur rem spectemus, certitudo salutis quoad hanc vel illam personam singularem niti debet decreto aliquo Dei practico infallibiliter decernente et operante salutem ejusdem. Si certam rei cognitionem quoad nos: certitudo salutis nostrae niti debet revelatione aliqua ejusdem decreti, per Spiritum adoptionis, et effecta ejusdem in cordibus singulorum. Nam Spiritus ille testificatur spiritui nostro nos esse illos Dei filios, quos destinavit aeternae vitae, quosque sanctificavit in hoc saeculo, ut possit glorificare in futuro. Caeterum in illo universali decreto per modum legis promulgato, Quisquis crediderit salvus erit, nec certa salus cujusquam singularis personae fundari potest, nec certa cognitio cujusquam de salute sua infallibiliter futura. Atque haec sunt omnia illa argumenta, quibus Collocutores conati sunt stabilire electionem hominum singularium ex antecedanea fidei praevisae conditione. Quae omnia ex Arminii scriptis desumpta sunt.
